extracted.intended_audience: Authors and teams preparing Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of healthcare interventions, covering standard methods (planning, searching, selection, data collection, bias assessment, analysis, GRADE, interpretation) and specialised topics (non-randomized studies, adverse effects, complex interventions, equity, economics, PROMs, IPD, prospective meta-analysis, qualitative research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on planning a review is included as a standard method applicable to every review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook is the official guide describing in detail the process of preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews on the effects of healthcare interventions; all authors should consult the Handbook for guidance on planning a review. See the relevant Handbook chapters (and linked MECIR items) for procedural expectations and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on searching for studies and selecting eligible studies for inclusion in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides standard methods for searching and selecting studies that are applicable to every Cochrane review. Authors should follow chapter guidance on comprehensive search strategies, selection processes, documentation, and reproducibility; related MECIR core standards collate key expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on data collection from included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook describes standard methods for data collection (what data to extract, extraction procedures, double extraction, managing missing data, data management). Authors should follow chapter procedures to ensure accurate, reproducible data capture and link to MECIR items where core standards are summarised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on assessing risk of bias in included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes methods for risk of bias assessment (tools and approaches suitable for randomized and non-randomized studies). Authors should apply recommended tools and justify judgments; see linked MECIR core standards for expectations on reporting and conduct of bias assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on statistical analysis methods for synthesising study data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard statistical approaches (meta-analysis methods, model choice, heterogeneity assessment, sensitivity analyses) are covered. Authors should follow Handbook guidance to choose appropriate statistical methods, report analytic decisions, and assess robustness of findings; MECIR collates core expectations relating to analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides instruction on applying GRADE to rate the certainty/quality of evidence for outcomes. Authors should follow the Handbook's GRADE guidance when presenting summary of findings and interpreting evidence certainty; MECIR items link to the GRADE-related chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interpretation of review results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook covers how to interpret findings, including consideration of effect sizes, certainty (GRADE), clinical importance, applicability, and limitations. Authors should use the Handbook to frame conclusions appropriately and transparently report implications for practice and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on conducting and interpreting reviews that include non-randomized studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes specific methods for non-randomized studies (design-specific considerations, bias assessment, confounding). Authors conducting reviews that include non-randomized evidence should consult the relevant specialised chapters for appropriate methods and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on identifying, extracting, analysing and interpreting adverse effects (harms) data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides methods tailored to adverse effects (searching for harms, data collection, synthesis, interpretation). Authors should follow this guidance when harms are important to the review question and report methods and findings transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance for reviews of complex interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook addresses specific methodological challenges for complex interventions (heterogeneity of intervention components, context, implementation). Authors should consult these chapters to design eligible criteria, synthesis approaches, and interpretation strategies suitable for complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on considering equity in systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes methods for identifying and analysing equity-relevant questions and subgroups, and for interpreting findings with respect to health equity. Authors should follow these methods when equity is a focus of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on incorporating economic evidence and cost-effectiveness considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook contains chapters on economic methods (searching for economic studies, data extraction, synthesis). Authors integrating economic evidence should use the Handbook's methods to ensure appropriate identification, analysis, and interpretation of economic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes (PROMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on dealing with patient-reported outcomes in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on selection, measurement, synthesis, and interpretation of patient-reported outcome measures. Authors should apply recommended approaches to ensure PROMs are handled consistently and meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data (IPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on conducting reviews using individual patient data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides methods for IPD meta-analyses (data collection from investigators, data checking, analysis). Authors planning IPD reviews should follow these specialised chapters for conduct and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on prospective meta-analysis methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook covers methods for prospective meta-analysis (pre-specification, coordination, analysis). Authors planning or conducting a prospective meta-analysis should consult these chapters for standards and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance on incorporating qualitative research in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes methods for locating, appraising, synthesising, and interpreting qualitative evidence relevant to intervention reviews. Authors including qualitative evidence should follow these chapters for appropriate methodology and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR) core standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance are collated as the Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR), which provide core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item provides a concise core standard and includes a link to the relevant Handbook chapter. MECIR items summarise essential expectations for conduct and reporting of Cochrane reviews; authors should consult MECIR alongside the full Handbook chapters to ensure compliance with Cochrane's methodological standards.
